# Test fixtures

All media here is synthetic and generated by this repository's tooling. Nothing is
sampled from a third-party recording, so there is no external licence: the files
are released under the same terms as the repository (fictional demo data).

## `reply.mp3` (fake TTS output)

- Source: ffmpeg `lavfi` 440 Hz sine generator, authored once on 2026-10-23 with
  `ffmpeg 7.1.1-1ubuntu1.3` (fixture-authoring tooling only; ffmpeg is **not** an
  application, CI or runtime requirement once this file is committed).
- Command:

  ```bash
  ffmpeg -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=1:sample_rate=24000 -ac 1 -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 64k tests/fixtures/reply.mp3
  ```

- Format (ffprobe): MP3 (ID3v2 header + MPEG audio frames), mono, 24 kHz, 64 kb/s,
  duration about 1.06 s, 8684 bytes. It is a real MP3, not a WAV renamed to `.mp3`.
- SHA-256: `8c095196419c3da13ed324f8f65a22e5f39504475b110374cdc3e13abbed1bc3`
- Used by: `tests/support/fakes.py::reply_mp3_bytes()`, returned by the E2E fake
  `synthesize`; the application serves it unchanged as `audio/mpeg`.

## Generated WAV fixtures (not committed; created per test)

Generator: `tests/support/fakes.py::make_wav(rate, channels, width, seconds, peak, silent)`
using the standard-library `wave` and `struct` modules. The signal is a square wave
of exactly +/- `peak` (period 40 frames), or all zeros when `silent=True`, so the bytes
are deterministic.

| Fixture | Call | Properties | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| valid upload | `make_wav()` | 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM, 1.0 s, peak 1000, 32044 bytes | `b0d37d5e191ec3a1aac79f780279c4180573be25c4e53a4844e6690a515c51e7` |
| silence | `make_wav(silent=True)` | same format, all-zero samples, 32044 bytes | `643f8a8dc8bd9c19225afffad2becfec5426180b3749cb208abdf1a6c8354efc` |

Boundary files use the same generator with explicit `rate`, `channels`, `width` and
`seconds` arguments.

## Fake STT text

The E2E fake `transcribe` returns `Order NS-000123 arrived broken and this is urgent`
unless a test scripts a different text.
